advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Scope the transition-hint JQL to the probed project (add `project = "<KEY>"`) by threading project_key into _transition_hints.
evidence: `jql = f'issuetype = "{issue_type}" ORDER BY created DESC'` in `_transition_hints` — the JQL never references `project_key`/`key`
`build_mapping_layer` passes only `issue_types` (names) into `_transition_hints(port, issue_types)`, so the project key is not even available to scope the search
advisory.finding: `_transition_hints` builds `jql = f'issuetype = "{issue_type}" ORDER BY created DESC'` with NO `project = <KEY>` clause, so the sampled issues (and thus the transition hints and their source statuses) are drawn from the entire Jira instance rather than the project being probed.
scenarios: A shared Jira with many projects: transition hints for project REB come from whichever project happens to have the most-recently-created issue of that type, misrepresenting REB's workflow
advisory.suggested_fix: Pass project_key into `_transition_hints` and build `jql = f'project = "{key}" AND issuetype = "{issue_type}" ORDER BY created DESC'`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Escape or reject double-quotes in issue-type names before interpolating into the transition-hint JQL.
evidence: `jql = f'issuetype = "{issue_type}" ORDER BY created DESC'` interpolates `issue_type` without escaping embedded quotes
`search_issues` is wrapped by `_soft`, so a JQL parse error degrades to `[]` invisibly
advisory.finding: Issue-type / project-key values containing a double-quote are interpolated raw into JQL (`issuetype = "{issue_type}"`), producing malformed JQL for such names; combined with the fail-soft catch, the search silently returns nothing rather than a hint.
scenarios: A Jira issue type named e.g. `Bug "critical"` yields malformed JQL and no transition hints, with no diagnostic

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that monkeypatches build_probe (or the layer builder) to raise and asserts suggest-mapping returns 1 with the 'could not probe Jira project' stderr message.
evidence: Handler: `except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - surface any probe failure as a clean UX error` writing `f"Error: could not probe Jira project {key!r}: {exc}\n"` then `return 1`
The fake port (_FakePort) never raises from a read getter, and no test monkeypatches build_probe to raise; no test asserts a return code of 1 from suggest-mapping.
ABSENCE: no test in tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_probe.py drives the probe-failure branch or asserts exit code 1 / the error message.
advisory.finding: The probe-failure error path in _bridge_suggest_mapping (build_probe/build_mapping_layer raising -> stderr 'Error: could not probe Jira project ...' + return code 1) has no test. A regression that swallowed the exception or returned 0 would go undetected; the whole error UX (nonzero exit, actionable message) is unverified.
scenarios: A live probe hits a bad project key or missing JIRA_URL/JIRA_PAT and must exit 1 with a diagnostic.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test: monkeypatch mapping_probe.build_probe to raise RuntimeError('boom'); assert main([...]) == 1 and 'could not probe Jira project' in capsys.readouterr().err.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test with a fake port whose issue_types omit hierarchyLevel (and/or an empty axis) asserting 'hierarchy' is absent and the corresponding _notes honesty message is emitted.
evidence: _honesty_notes appends 'hierarchy omitted: no issue type reported a hierarchyLevel' only `if not hierarchy:`

build_mapping_layer only sets `layer["_notes"] = notes` and drops `hierarchy` when empty; the fake supplies hierarchyLevel for every type (_ISSUE_TYPES has hierarchyLevel 1/0/-1), so the empty-hierarchy branch is never hit.
ABSENCE: no test uses a fake port with empty/omitted-hierarchy vocabulary to assert the hierarchy key is dropped and the honesty note is emitted.
advisory.finding: The fail-soft empty-axis behavior and the _honesty_notes / _notes emission are untested. The fake port always returns full vocabulary (issue_types, statuses, hierarchyLevel, hints), so the empty-vocabulary _notes path and the 'hierarchy omitted' note branch (emitted only when hierarchy is empty) never execute.
scenarios: Data Center Jira returns no hierarchyLevel; a 403 makes an axis empty and the note must be emitted rather than a fabricated value.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a --write test in a project with no existing rebar.toml asserting the file is created containing the [mapping.projects.<KEY>] block.
evidence: `target = proj[0] if (proj is not None and proj[1] == "toml") else base / "rebar.toml"` then `if target.is_file(): ... else data = {}` and later mkdir + atomic replace.
test_probe_write_preserves_edits pre-writes `rebar_toml.write_text(...)` before invoking --write, so target.is_file() is always True in the only --write test.
ABSENCE: no test invokes --write in a project with no rebar.toml to verify a new file is created with the [mapping.projects.<KEY>] block.
advisory.finding: The --write branch that CREATES a new rebar.toml at <repo_root>/rebar.toml (no pre-existing config) is untested. test_probe_write_preserves_edits only covers the case where rebar.toml already exists.
scenarios: An operator runs suggest-mapping --write in a repo that has no rebar.toml yet.

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Have build_mapping_layer/the probe assert at least one getter actually succeeded (e.g. non-empty issue_types or statuses) and surface an error/exit-1 when a probe produced nothing, so total probe failure is distinguishable from an empty project.
evidence: `except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - fail-soft on any external getter (advisory tool)` then `return default` in `_JiraProbePort._soft`

In `_bridge_suggest_mapping` the only guard is `except Exception as exc:` around `build_probe()`/`build_mapping_layer`, but the port swallows getter failures internally so `build_mapping_layer` never raises — an all-403 run still returns 0 with an empty block
`_honesty_notes` always returns >=2 notes, so a non-empty `_notes` is emitted even when every getter failed, further masking the difference
blocking.finding: The probe port's `_soft` wrapper catches every exception and returns an empty default, so a whole-probe failure (bad credentials/403 on every getter, nonexistent project key, or network outage) is silently indistinguishable from a genuinely empty project: `build_mapping_layer` never raises, the CLI emits a mapping block with empty vocabulary/identity maps, and the command exits 0 reporting apparent success. The check cannot distinguish 'probed and clean' from 'probe never succeeded'.
scenarios: Operator runs `rebar bridge suggest-mapping REB` with expired/insufficient Jira credentials and receives an empty [mapping] block that looks like a valid suggestion
Operator mistypes the project key; every createmeta/search call 403s or 404s and the tool emits empty maps + notes, exit 0
